title: 652 Nanoseconds to Catch Your Local Model Guessing
description: Ask your local model the same question three times and compare the answers: agreement means trust, scatter means guessing. Spanda turns that comparison into a 652.1-nanosecond CPU computation, a gateway beside Ollama that stamps every reply. All benchmark numbers are the author's own and unreplicated.
hook_text: Six hundred fifty-two nanoseconds. Spanda just ratted your local model out.
hook_candidates: Six hundred fifty-two nanoseconds. Spanda just ratted your local model out.

A millionth of a second to catch a guessing model.
Your Ollama isn't lying. Its memory of facts is.
Ninety thousand times faster, and the GPU is optional.
Spanda: a Rust gateway that stamps every guess your model makes.
Zero GPU. One CPU core. Every reply stamped.
Your local model has a tell. It's free to check.
Semantic entropy caught hallucinations. It needed a second brain.
Three answers, one question: that's the whole lie detector.
narration_full: Six hundred fifty-two nanoseconds. Spanda just ratted your local model out. You run Ollama on your PC; every answer sounds equally sure. That calm hides epistemic uncertainty, the model's own lack of knowledge. Ask the same question three times, like three friends asked separately. Agreement means trust; scatter means guessing. Semantic entropy, the established detector, compares meanings with a second neural network. Its judge burns ninety-two thousand four hundred microseconds per query. Spanda, a small gateway, matches exact text, no GPU. It sits beside Ollama at two point nine eight megabytes, stamping every reply. One pip install tonight; the stamp stays on. The catch: your model still writes all three answers first. And a tuned giant repeats one wrong answer every time, Confident Mode Collapse. Agreement is evidence, not truth.

analogy.vehicle: asking three friends the same question separately
analogy.mapping: the three sampled answers are three separate askings of one model; identical answers mean trust, scattered answers mean it was guessing, and the comparison itself is nearly free
analogy.limit: the three friends share one brain, so a heavily tuned model can repeat the same wrong answer every time
